verdict: Nuclear's demand case remains strong, but the investable signal is still execution: the global fleet is about 400 GWe with about 75 reactors under construction, at least five DOE-authorised test reactors have now reached criticality (Oklo's Groves on August 6, with Westinghouse's eVinci completing cold criticality testing at NCERC on August 25), and DOE conditionally committed $17.5B for ten 1.1 GW AP1000s. None of those advanced-build milestones is commercial capacity yet. Uranium firmed to $89.85/lb, while HALEU remains constrained despite new Centrus-X-Energy prepayment contracting. Existing fleets, restarts, and fuel-cycle bottlenecks still offer the clearest risk-adjusted exposure; advanced developers remain execution-heavy.

players.name: Constellation Energy
players.category: Nuclear fleet and clean power PPAs
players.role: Largest pure-play U.S. nuclear generation platform.
players.exposure: Existing fleet, Crane restart, and large corporate PPAs make it the clearest public-market nuclear utility proxy.

players.name: Vistra
players.role: Independent power producer with nuclear assets and data-center contracting exposure.
players.exposure: Nuclear output is becoming more valuable as hyperscalers pay for firm clean power.

players.name: Cameco
players.role: Major uranium producer and strategic nuclear-services owner.
players.exposure: Levered to uranium contracting, mine restarts, and the Westinghouse reactor-services platform.

players.name: BWX Technologies
players.role: Specialized nuclear manufacturing, services, and defense nuclear supplier.
players.exposure: More industrial and defense nuclear than merchant power; lower concept risk than pre-revenue reactor developers.
players.source: Stock Analysis, BWX Technologies market cap

players.name: Oklo
players.exposure: High optionality but high execution and licensing risk; no commercial reactor fleet yet.

players.name: Uranium Energy
players.exposure: Tied to uranium price, contracting, and restart or development execution rather than reactor sales.
players.source: Stock Analysis, Uranium Energy market cap

players.name: NuScale Power
players.role: Certified U.S. SMR technology with commercialization risk.
players.exposure: Regulatory first-mover status matters, but project economics and customer conversion remain the proof points.

players.name: Centrus Energy
players.role: Nuclear fuel-cycle and enrichment bottleneck exposure.
players.exposure: Strategically important if advanced reactors need domestic HALEU at commercial scale.

players.name: Microsoft / Constellation
players.role: 20-year PPA supporting the restart of the Crane Clean Energy Center.
players.exposure: Near-term nuclear growth may come from restarts and uprates before new SMRs arrive.

players.name: Google / Kairos Power
players.role: Corporate agreement for multiple Kairos deployments through 2035.
players.exposure: Hyperscalers are willing to contract ahead of commercial advanced-reactor maturity.

players.name: Amazon / X-energy
players.role: Cascade project with Energy Northwest and Xe-100 reactors.
players.exposure: Large enough to matter for data centers, but still depends on licensing, financing, and construction.

players.name: Meta nuclear portfolio
players.role: Agreements across existing and new nuclear to support AI power demand.
players.exposure: Nuclear is being bought as firm clean capacity, not only as branding.

metrics.label: Operating capacity
metrics.detail: The World Nuclear Association counts 440 operable power reactors totaling about 400 GWe across more than 30 countries. Nuclear supplies about 9% of global electricity.

metrics.label: Under construction
metrics.detail: About 75 reactors are under construction worldwide alongside the operable fleet. The pipeline is a long-duration buildout, not near-term generating capacity.

metrics.label: Planned U.S. builds
metrics.detail: DOE conditionally committed financing for long-lead items at five two-reactor sites. Each site still needs partner equity and final loan conditions before funding.

metrics.label: Uranium price
metrics.context: 28 Aug; +3.75% on the month; +17.22% year over year
metrics.detail: Trading Economics reported uranium at $89.85/lb on 28 August. This figure is a dated snapshot, not a live quote in the desktop app.

metrics.label: HALEU availability
metrics.context: Centrus–X-energy prepayments; no U.S. commercial output yet
metrics.detail: A Centrus–X-energy enrichment and prepayment agreement eases the funding problem and backs a contingent LEU/HALEU backlog, but there is still no commercial domestic HALEU source in production.

metrics.label: Hyperscaler pull
metrics.detail: The IEA expects data-centre electricity consumption to roughly double from 485 TWh in 2025 to 950 TWh in 2030, which strengthens the case for firm clean power.

signals.label: Restarts and uprates are the near-term path
signals.summary: Holtec reports that Palisades has completed its major restart projects and shifted to maintenance, testing, inspection, and operational readiness. More than 5,000 activities remain before fuel load and startup.
signals.watch: Watch fuel load, remaining NRC approvals, the startup milestone, and Crane's 2027 restart schedule.

signals.label: SMRs are demand-backed but not yet routine infrastructure
signals.summary: TerraPower began Natrium construction after NRC approval and contracted Doosan Enerbility for equipment at Kemmerer. Westinghouse completed zero-power criticality testing of a one-fifth-scale eVinci reactor at NCERC. Commercial economics remain unproven.
signals.watch: Watch equipment deliveries, TerraPower's planned Part 50 filing, and whether test-reactor results convert into licensed commercial plants.

signals.label: Advanced fuel is a gating item
signals.summary: Standard Nuclear reports construction substantially complete at its Tennessee and Idaho TRISO sites, and Centrus and X-energy signed an enrichment and prepayment agreement. Supply still has to start at commercial volume.
signals.watch: Watch TRISO startup, initial MTU output, and whether Centrus's Piketon expansion delivers contracted volumes.

signals.label: Hyperscalers are becoming anchor customers
signals.summary: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft have all signed nuclear PPAs that could provide about 6.9 GW by the early 2030s. Projects still face regulatory and construction dependencies.
signals.watch: Watch named sites, binding offtake, NRC and interconnection progress, and whether 2027 restart targets become firm milestones.

signals.label: Supply-chain geopolitics define the investable map
signals.summary: DOE's conditional loan package targets ten new large reactors through up to five loans for five two-reactor sites. The financing supports long-lead items, not funded builds, until partners, equity, and final conditions are in place.
signals.watch: Watch partner names, final loan conditions, equity commitments, and long-lead purchase orders.

signals.label: Licensing and waste remain public-trust constraints
signals.summary: The NRC has proposed revisions to ALARA and reactor-licensing requirements, and DOE amended WIPP's record of decision to add disposal panels and extend the operating horizon. Siting, waste, and public trust remain separate constraints.
signals.watch: Watch the comment process, final NRC rules, court challenges, and WIPP panel excavation.
